name: Centro Historico
tagline: The living heart of medieval Guimaraes
description: The UNESCO old town of granite lanes and squares like the Largo da Oliveira and Praca de Santiago, packed with cafes, shops and history. Walkable, atmospheric and central, it is where most visitors and nomads want to base themselves.
bestFor: Nomads who want atmosphere, cafes and everything within an easy walk
pros: Beautiful UNESCO squares on your doorstep

name: Colina Sagrada (Castle Hill)
tagline: Castle, palace and Portugal's founding hill
description: The Sacred Hill crowned by the tenth-century Guimaraes Castle and the Palace of the Dukes of Braganca, where the wall reads Aqui nasceu Portugal. A green, monumental edge of the old town, calm and steeped in the nation's origins.
bestFor: History lovers wanting calm, greenery and iconic landmarks nearby
pros: Beside the castle and ducal palace

name: Couros and Campus (Azurem)
tagline: University energy and creative tannery quarter
description: The student-flavoured area around the old Couros tannery quarter and the university campuses, now a hub of creativity, startups and casual bars. Younger, more affordable and buzzing during term, with a working, forward-looking feel beside the heritage.
bestFor: Younger nomads and students wanting affordability, energy and casual nights

name: Penha and Creixomil outskirts
description: The leafy outskirts stretching toward the Penha hill and the Creixomil residential district, reached by cable car or a short bus ride. Quieter and greener, with more space, trails and everyday living away from the tourist bustle of the centre.
bestFor: Those wanting space, nature and quiet with the centre a ride away
pros: Nature and the Penha cable car nearby
cons: Rely more on buses or the cable car
